title: VPC DNS Resolution Failure
symptom: Instances in VPC cannot resolve public domain names or private Route 53 zones; `nslookup` times out.
initial_observations: Ping to public IP (8.8.8.8) succeeds, but domain lookups fail.

possible_causes.cause: VPC attribute `enableDnsSupport` is set to false
possible_causes.remediation: Enable DNS support: `aws ec2 modify-vpc-attribute --vpc-id vpc-xxx --enable-dns-support '{"Value": true}'`.

possible_causes.cause: Custom DHCP option set points to unreachable external DNS servers
possible_causes.evidence_needed: cat /etc/resolv.conf points to non-Amazon IP that drops traffic.
possible_causes.remediation: Update DHCP option set to use AmazonProvidedDNS or valid corporate forwarder.

investigation_steps.title: Check VPC DNS Attributes
investigation_steps.command: aws ec2 describe-vpc-attribute --vpc-id vpc-xxxx --attribute enableDnsSupport && aws ec2 describe-vpc-attribute --vpc-id vpc-xxxx --attribute enableDnsHostnames
investigation_steps.explanation: Verify both DNS support and DNS hostnames are enabled on the VPC.

investigation_steps.title: Check Guest OS /etc/resolv.conf Configuration
investigation_steps.explanation: Confirm nameserver points to the AmazonProvidedDNS (VPC base + 2 or 169.254.169.253).
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: nameserver entry matching VPC CIDR base + 2.

verification: Run `dig amazon.com` and confirm NOERROR status with valid Answer section.
prevention: Ensure IaC templates (Terraform/CloudFormation) explicitly set `enable_dns_support = true`.
